stories.headline: 'Some dishes are best served cold': Top LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in encounter in J&K's Kulgam
stories.bodyText:
Refused to surrender, opened fire: LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in Kulgam
NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most wanted terrorist Lateef Bhat was killed by security forces on Wednesday, hours after an encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, news agency PTI reported.
Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir following specific intelligence inputs. Officials said Bhat was trapped inside the cordon and was repeatedly urged to lay down his arms.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

stories.headline: फांसी की सजा पर रस्साकशी : मृत्युदंड पर रोक के खिलाफ भारत का मतदान
stories.deck: मृत्युदंड के लिए एक ऐसी आपराधिक न्याय प्रणाली की जरूरत होती है जिसमें गलती की गुंजाइश न के बराबर हो
stories.bodyText:
संयुक्त राष्ट्र में प्रस्तावित मौत की सजा पर दुनिया भर में रोक के खिलाफ भारत का मतदान, इस मंच पर उसके रुख के अनुरूप है। भारत ने मौत की सजा को बनाए रखने का बचाव करते हुए इसे एक संप्रभु फैसला बताया है, जिसे न्यायिक सुरक्षा उपायों का समर्थन हासिल है। इन उपायों में ‘दुर्लभतम से दुर्लभ’ मामला होने की शर्त और सत्र अदालतों द्वारा दी गई सजा पर हाईकोर्ट की मुहर की जरूरत शामिल है। साथ ही, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मृत्युदंड को लगातार सीमित किया है और शोध में ऐसा कोई सबूत नहीं मिला है जिससे यह साबित हो सके कि मौत की सजा, आजीवन कारावास के मुकाबले अपराध रोकने में ज्यादा कारगर है। भारत में न्यायिक फांसी और गैर-न्यायिक हत्याओं के बीच का अंतर कानूनी रूप से तो सही है, लेकिन यह दावा उतना सही नहीं है कि ‘उचित कानूनी प्रक्रिया’ फांसी का सामना कर रहे लोगों को सुरक्षा प्रदान करती है। भारत में आखिरी बार 2020 में दिल्ली गैंगरेप और हत्या के दोषियों को फांसी दी गई थी। इसके बावजूद, संसद ने ‘भारतीय न्याय संहिता’ के तहत मौत की सजा वाले अपराधों की संख्या बढ़ा दी है। यह एक किस्म का ‘दंडात्मक लोकलुभावनवाद’ है, जिसमें सरकार जनता के आक्रोश को शांत करने के लिए ऐसे कदम उठाती है जो राजनीतिक रूप से आकर्षक लगते हैं - खासकर यौन हिंसा के मामलों में। लेकिन, इन कदमों से पुलिस व्यवस्था की कमियों या सजा दिलाने की कम दर जैसी असली समस्याओं का समाधान नहीं होता, जो वास्तव में अपराध रोकने के असर को कमजोर करती हैं। देश में 31 दिसंबर 2025 तक 574 लोग ऐसे थे जिन्हें मौत की सजा सुनाई गई थी। वर्ष 2016 के बाद से यह तादाद सबसे ज्यादा है। इसका कारण निचली अदालत (ट्रायल कोर्ट) के फैसले हैं, जो न्यायिक सुरक्षा उपायों के व्यावहारिक दावों पर सवाल उठाते हैं। न्यायमूर्ति ए.पी. शाह की अध्यक्षता वाले 2015 के विधि आयोग की रिपोर्ट में कहा गया है कि मौत की सजा “संवैधानिक रूप से मान्य किसी भी दंड-संबंधी लक्ष्य को हासिल करने में नाकाम” रहती है। रिपोर्ट में आतंकवाद और युद्ध छेड़ने जैसे अपराधों को छोड़कर, बाकी सभी अपराधों के लिए मौत की सजा को खत्म करने की सिफारिश की गई थी।
दुनिया भर में सिर्फ कुछ ही देश ऐसे हैं जहां लोगों को मौत की सजा दी जा रही है। ‘प्रोजेक्ट 39 ए’ के अनुसार, भारत में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 2016-2025 के बीच मौत की सजा पाए 38 लोगों को रिहा किया। ये लोग औसतन आठ साल तक मौत की सजा के इंतजार में जेल में रहे थे। इनमें से कुछ ने तो दो दशक से भी ज्यादा वक्त तक यह पीड़ा झेली है। इस सजा के लिए कभी गलती न होने की गुंजाइश की जरूरत होती है, जिसे हमारी आपराधिक न्याय प्रणाली प्रदान नहीं कर सकती। ये सुरक्षा उपाय न तो दोषपूर्ण सबूतों या झूठी गवाही जैसे मामलों में गलत सजा को रोक पाते हैं और न ही सजा का सामना कर रहे लोगों के लिए सक्षम कानूनी मदद तक समान पहुंच सुनिश्चित कर पाते हैं। भारत को औपचारिक रूप से फांसी की सजा पर रोक लगा देनी चाहिए और सजा से जुड़े कानूनों तथा मौत की सजा पाए कैदियों के साथ होने वाले बर्ताव की समीक्षा करानी चाहिए। दूसरी बात, जिन अपराधों में जानबूझकर हत्या नहीं की गई है, उन्हें इस सजा के दायरे से बाहर रखा जाना चाहिए। शोध बताते हैं कि जानलेवा न होने वाले अपराधों के लिए बहुत कठोर सजा देने से अपराधी और ज्यादा हिंसक हो सकते हैं। वे गवाहों को भी मार सकते हैं। हमारा मुख्य लक्ष्य कानून से इस प्रथा को पूरी तरह खत्म करना होना चाहिए और साथ ही जांच-पड़ताल, अभियोजन की प्रक्रियाओं और कानूनी सहायता की बेहतर तरीके से सुलभ कराना चाहिए।

stories.headline: The expansion of Bhagyalakshmi Temple near Hyderabad’s Charminar | Explained
stories.deck: One of the first letters the ASI wrote to the Commission of Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad was on December 13, 1968, alerting the civic body of the construction
stories.bodyText:
The story so far: The Bhagyalakshmi Temple near Charminar in Hyderabad — a small temple built sometime after 1959 — has now expanded to cover much of the nationally protected monument’s south-eastern flank.
This Deepavali, the site became the epicenter of massive gridlock after temple officials began distributing free “silver coins” on November 8. About five lakh visitors from all corners of the city reached the temple on the three days of Deepavali, police officials said. However, devotees who queued up for the tokens, which is stamped with the temple’s name against a backdrop of the Charminar, have pointed out that the coins appeared to be made of aluminium.

stories.headline: High-fives! Pakistan give India guard of honour after SAFF final - Watch
stories.deck: After the SAFF Championship final, Pakistan's football team provided India with a guard of honour, showcasing sportsmanship. India won the final 2-1, securing their 10th SAFF title. The match featured a significant red card for Pakistan, which altered the game's dynamics. Both teams displayed mutual respect during the medal ceremony, emphasizing a positive spirit in football. This display…
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan's footballers showed a fine example of sportsmanship by giving India a guard of honour after the SAFF Championship final in Dhaka on Tuesday. India had beaten Pakistan 2-1 to lift the trophy, but the gesture from the losing team stood out amid the strained sporting relations between the two neighbours in recent times.
After the final, Pakistani players lined up to applaud the Indian champions. Players from both teams also shook hands and exchanged high-fives during the medal ceremony. The scenes were in sharp contrast to the refusal to shake hands that has become common in India-Pakistan cricket matches.
Football offers a different picture
The no-handshake practice has been seen regularly in India-Pakistan cricket matches since the 2025 Asia Cup. Players from both sides have skipped the customary greetings at the toss as well as after matches. The practice has extended to both men's and women's competitions.
It began after the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025 and the military escalation that followed. The trend continued at the 2025 Asia Cup, the Under-19 Asia Cup, the Women's World Cup and the Women's Asia Cup in 2026.
The same was seen at the Asian Games in Japan last month, where India captain Shreyas Iyer and Pakistan skipper Sahibzada Farhan did not shake hands at the toss before the men's cricket final.
WATCH:
Football, however, provided a different example.
The two teams had exchanged greetings earlier in the tournament as well. Before their group-stage match on November 5, India head coach Naushad Moosa had indicated that his players would follow the customary pre-match greetings. India captain Bijoy Varghese then shook hands with Pakistan skipper Yousuf Ijaz Butt.
The guard of honour after Tuesday's final was another strong display of sporting spirit. The players from both teams also shared handshakes and high-fives during the medal ceremony after an intense contest.
Sporting gestures also seen at Asian Games
There were similar displays of sportsmanship at the Asian Games, where Indian and Pakistani athletes exchanged greetings in hockey, volleyball, table tennis and squash despite tensions between the two countries.
Indian hockey players shook hands with their Pakistani opponents after a dramatic semifinal. In volleyball, Pakistani players were seen consoling their Indian opponents after securing a victory.
India fight back to win 10th SAFF title
India had to come from behind to beat Pakistan 2-1 and claim their 10th SAFF Championship title. The win also helped the team complete a hat-trick of consecutive titles.
Pakistan, who were playing their first-ever SAFF final, took the lead through Alamgir Ghazi in first-half stoppage time.
India found it difficult to settle in the first half but received a major boost when Junaid Shah was sent off in the 59th minute. The red card followed a VAR review of his dangerous challenge on Brison Fernandes.
India capitalised on their numerical advantage. Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored the equaliser in the 60th minute, while Sandip Mandi found the net in the 88th minute to seal the victory.
The 2026 SAFF Championship, the main men's football competition for South Asian national teams, featured six countries. India competed with a second-string squad consisting mostly of younger players under U-23 coach Naushad Moosa, instead of its first-choice senior team.

briefs.headline: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
briefs.deck: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government
briefs.bodyText:
Three weeks after President Lula da Silva’s election victory, Brazilian institutions are tightening the screws on Big Tech over alleged interference in favour of his far-right rival Flávio Bolsonaro during the campaign. The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference from outside through digital platforms. We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula told his supporters after winning the election on October 25.
On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the Brazilian government stepped up efforts to pass a bill which would give the country’s competition regulator (CADE) more powers to monitor the Big Tech operations. Pending since September 2025, the bill is modelled on European Union regulations and it faces opposition from Bolsonaro allies.

briefs.headline: शांति की कठिन डगरः जम्मू-कश्मीर में आतंकवादी हमले
briefs.deck: जम्मू-कश्मीर में अमन के लिए राज्य का दर्जा बहाल करना जरूरी
briefs.bodyText:
जम्मू-कश्मीर में सुरक्षा बलों ने तीन महीनों से जो सुकून कायम कर रखा था उसमें पिछले छह दिनों में हिंसा की ताबड़तोड़ घटनाओं से खलल पड़ गया। बीते 11 नवंबर को, कुलगाम में एक नाके पर तैनात केंद्रीय रिजर्व पुलिस बल (सीआरपीएफ) के कर्मियों पर आतंकी हमला हुआ जिसमें तीन जवान घायल हो गये। 16 नवंबर को, कुलगाम के रिहाइशी इलाकों में छह दिनों तक चले घेराबंदी-नुमा आतंकवाद-विरोधी अभियान के बाद, एक स्थानीय व्यक्ति मारा गया, जिसके बारे में पुलिस को शक था कि वह चंद दिनों पहले ही आतंकवादी संगठन में शामिल हुआ है। जम्मू के किश्तवाड़ में, जम्मू-कश्मीर पुलिस के दो विशेष पुलिस अधिकारी (एसपीओ) गोलियों के जख्म के साथ मृत पाये गये, जिसके एक दिन पहले 11 नवंबर को इन्हें एक वन क्षेत्र से लापता बताया गया था। इन एसपीओ की हत्या की परिस्थितियों को लेकर पुलिस और सेना ने होंठ सिल रखे हैं और किन परिस्थितियों में वे मौत के मुंह में पहुंचे, इस पर विरोधाभासी खबरें सामने आ रही हैं। कुलगाम के रिहाइशी इलाकों में आतंकवाद-विरोधी अभियान ने चिंताएं पैदा कर दी हैं। जम्मू-कश्मीर की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री और पीडीपी अध्यक्ष महबूबा मुफ्ती ने छह दिनों तक चले इस अभियान को “केवल परायापन और नाराजगी पैदा करने वाली सामूहिक सजा” करार दिया, जबकि नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस के प्रवक्ता इमरान नबी डार ने कहा कि पूरे-पूरे गांवों को कई दिन लंबी पाबंदियों में रखा गया। साल 2019 से केंद्रशासित प्रदेश बने जम्मू-कश्मीर में, सीमित शक्तियों और पुलिस पर कोई अधिकार न होने के कारण, उमर अब्दुल्ला सरकार खुद को लाचार पाती है। सिर्फ सुरक्षा के लिहाज से बात करें तो आतंकवाद और अलगाववाद के खात्मे की कठोर नीति कारगर रही है — आतंकी हमलों के साथ-साथ आतंकी संगठनों में स्थानीय लोगों की भर्ती में कमी आयी है। पुलिस के मुताबिक, कश्मीर में आतंकी संगठनों में भर्ती होने वाले स्थानीय लोगों की संख्या घटकर एक अंक में या 10 से कम रह गयी है।
फिर भी, आतंकवादी घटनाओं में कमी और सड़कों पर खामोशी को शांति नहीं समझना चाहिए। वर्तमान स्थिति की मांग है कि केंद्र सरकार जम्मू-कश्मीर के सभी हितधारकों तक राजनीतिक रूप से पहुंचे। इसकी शुरुआत राज्य के दर्जे की बहाली से करनी होगी जिसका बार-बार वादा किया गया है। यह मतदाताओं में यह भाव जगायेगा कि विधानसभा चुनाव 2024 में उनकी भारी भागीदारी की बदौलत उनके चुने हुए नेता संस्थाओं को जवाबदेह ठहरा पाएं और वे इस क्षेत्र के हितों की रक्षा के लिए खुलकर काम कर सकें। सुरक्षा एजेंसियों को पाकिस्तान-समर्थित आतंकवाद पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने की जरूरत है, लेकिन यह कश्मीर के भीतर लोगों को फिर से मनोवैज्ञानिक जख्म देने की कीमत पर नहीं होना चाहिए। ऐसे ही छोड़ देने पर यह स्थिति बारूद के ढेर में बदल सकती है। राजनीतिक और सुरक्षा प्रक्रियाओं, दोनों के जरिए चंगाई के प्रयास एक-दूसरे के विरोधी नहीं, बल्कि पूरक होने चाहिए। जम्मू-कश्मीर की राजनीतिक जमात को अपना इख्तियार कायम करने देना और सुरक्षा एजेंसियों को चुनौतियों से निपटने के लिए जगह देना, ये दोनों बातें परस्पर विरोधी नहीं हैं।

briefs.headline: Thirupparankundram row: T.N. govt pushes for stay of HC order to avoid breach of peace
briefs.deck: The HC had confirmed an earlier order to the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple devasthanam or management body to light the Karthigai Deepam on a stone pillar located atop the Thirupparankundram Hill
briefs.bodyText:
The Tamil Nadu government urged the Supreme Court on Tuesday to stay a Madras High Court decision of January 2026 which confirmed its earlier order to the Arulmigu Subramaniswamy Temple devasthanam or management body to light the Karthigai Deepam on a stone pillar located atop the Thirupparankundram Hill.
The Division Bench of the High Court in January had upheld the earlier Single Judge order, while brushing aside fears expressed by the State that such an action would be a sure recipe for “disturbance of public tranquility and peace”, given the fact that the stone pillar was proximate to a dargah. The High Court had dismissed the fears as an “imaginary ghost”.
On Tuesday, senior advocate Shekhar Naphade, for the Tamil Nadu government, said the fear was very real, and status quo must remain until the State’s appeal against the January order was finally decided by the apex court.
The submission came in a more than an hour-long hearing before a Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi. The hearing would resume on November 18.
Senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, for the Commissioner of the State’s Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department, argued that the unsubstantiated claims about the “custom” of lighting a Karthigai Deepam on the Deepathoon made by the Hindu Dharma Parishad (which was the petitioner in the High Court) was “calculated to occasion a breach of peace upon a sensitive site with a recorded history of communal tension”.
Mr. Gupta, along with Tamil Nadu’s Additional Advocate General and senior advocate Prashanto Chandra Sen, submitted that there has never been any established practice, custom, or even a prior claim of lighting the Karthigai Deepam upon the summit of the Thirupparankundram Hill or on the stone pillar “now described as the Deepathoon”. They submitted that the Karthigai Deepam had been lit only at the Deepa Mandapam for over 150 years.
“So, it does not matter what is the custom, what the Sthanikars think… can just anything be done now… Is there any custom established by the petitioner which would entitle him to a mandamus to allow himself to light the lamp on the pillar or direct the Devasthanam to light it on top of the hill? If the petitioner claims such a right, the burden is on him [the parishad],” Mr. Gupta submitted.
Mr. Naphade said the petitioner wanted to light the lamp on the side of the dargah and not on the side of the temple.
“He wants to light the lamp on the right side. On the right side is the dargah and on the left is the temple. A natural division. As a result of the High Court order, the natural division would be upset. There is potential for disturbance of public peace,” Mr. Naphade submitted.
Mr. Sen argued that a High Court cannot direct the executive authority of a temple to introduce innovations regarding time and place of worship or conduct of rituals that would affect worshippers’ established rights and facilities.
Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the Madurai District Collector, submitted that the word ‘Deepathoon’ did “not arise at any point before the year 2025”.
He said the entire prayer of the petitioner before the High Court was that “there is a pillar. In my imagination this pillar is a religious place and ‘I want you, the court, to step in and allow me to light a lamp there’”.
A recent affidavit submitted by the HR&CE Department in the apex court said the conduct of daily poojas, festivals and observances of the customary rituals of the temple, including the manner and the place of lighting of the Karthigai Deepam, fell within the exclusive domain of the temple administration in accordance with the Agamas, the opinion of the Sthanikars and the 1959 Act, and not with any private association like the petitioner-parishad.
It said the ownership of the Hill by the temple had already been decreed and settled by a 1923 court decision. According to which, the temple had ownership and possession of the whole of the Hill and the Giri Veedhi (surrounding road) except certain areas like the assessed and occupied lands in the Nellithope, the steps leading up to the mosque, and the top of the rock on which the mosque and the flag-staff of the Muslims stood.

briefs.headline: 15,627 social media posts removed since UDF came into power, Kerala govt reveals in Assembly
briefs.deck: Some of the removed content included posts featuring Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Ministers, according to a disclosure by the State government in the Legislative Assembly.
briefs.bodyText:
The Kerala Police have received 4,201 complaints that sought action against objectionable social media content since the United Democratic Front (UDF) government assumed office. These have resulted in legal action in 3,472 cases and the removal of 15,627 posts and links from various platforms.
Some of the removed content included posts featuring Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Ministers, according to a disclosure by the State government in the Legislative Assembly.
The figures were provided by Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala in a written reply to a question raised by Xavier Chittilappilly, MLA. The disclosure assumes significance against the backdrop of Mr. Satheesan’s denial that his office or the government had asked Meta to remove news reports and social media posts critical of him or the government.
While the Home Minister’s reply does not establish any direct intervention by the Chief Minister or his office in seeking the removal of critical posts, it confirms that the Kerala Police had issued notices through the Centre’s Sahyog portal for taking down content.
According to the reply, the Cyber Operations wing and Cybercrime police stations have been conducting round-the-clock cyber patrolling and surveillance to identify and prevent cybercrimes and the circulation of fake information through social media. The complaints received are investigated, and notices are issued to the respective social media portals through the Sahyog portal.
Financial scams
The content removed included fraudulent financial schemes, morphed images and deepfakes, communal hate messages, obscene material, cyber bullying posts and fake social media accounts used to extort money from the public.
Among the financial fraud-related content were fake trading platforms, part-time job scams, unauthorised loan applications and online betting links. The police also initiated action against manipulated photographs and videos, including fabricated news content and deepfake visuals that targeted public representatives and others. Posts that could trigger law and order issues, including communal hate speech and fake messages intended to spread panic, were also removed.
Responding specifically to a question on the removal of news cards, photographs and videos that featured the Chief Minister and Ministers, the Home Minister said the police had issued notices to social media platforms under Rules 3(1)(d) and 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules and Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act. Such action was initiated when complaints were received from the public or when synthetically generated content, including artificially edited videos and morphed photographs, that could be removed under the IT Rules came to the police’s attention.

briefs.headline: India needs a comprehensive doctrine on space security
briefs.deck: India’s objective should not be to turn outer space into another arena of conflict, but to ensure that disruption in space does not translate into vulnerability on Earth
briefs.bodyText:
Space has transformed from a specialised domain of scientific exploration into an area which hosts essential infrastructure underpinning everyday life, economic activity and national security. Communications, navigation, weather forecasting, disaster management, agriculture, banking, logistics and critical infrastructure are increasingly dependent on satellites and space-enabled services. In India, space capabilities support the armed forces through communications, positioning, surveillance, timing and situational awareness. Space is therefore no longer a separate technological sector but an essential component of national resilience and strategic autonomy. As dependence expands, disruption can have consequences for markets, governance, security and society at large.
The character of threats in space is changing. Competition extends beyond the destruction of satellites to the disruption of the services they provide. Space systems can now be affected by jamming and spoofing that interfere with communications and navigation. Cyber interference can target satellite networks, ground stations and supporting infrastructure, while electronic warfare can degrade signals and reduce the reliability of space-enabled systems. Such methods can produce effects without physically damaging a spacecraft, making attribution and response more complex. The vulnerability lies not only in the satellite itself, but in the wider architecture connecting space assets to users on Earth. This shift from destruction to disruption has made space security a more complex challenge for states.

briefs.headline: Promised in 10 days, parcel to Canada took 28 days; courier firm ordered to pay Rs 58k
briefs.deck: A consumer commission in Haryana held a courier service accountable for a delayed shipment to Canada. The firm failed to deliver clothes and food items within the assured timeframe, causing significant loss for the complainant. The shipment took 28 days instead of the promised 10-12 days, making perishable items unusable. The commission ordered the courier company to compensate the complainant…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has held a courier company guilty of deficiency in service for delivering a shipment of clothes and edible items to Canada 28 days after accepting it, despite assuring delivery within 10-12 days.
The commission directed Brand House to pay Rs 48,400 towards the value of the edible items and courier charges. It also ordered the firm to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation and litigation costs.
In its November 5, 2026, order, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, 
Rohtak
, noted that the delay had defeated the purpose of sending the seasonal clothes and perishable food items to Canada.
Courier firm delays delivery of food items and clothes to Canada
According to the commission order, Surender Dhokal, a 47-year-old advocate from Rohtak, had booked the services of Brand House on January 29, 2025, to send clothes and edible items to Canada.
The shipment was booked on January 30, 2025, under tracking ID 1Z0V1Y572017007517. The complainant handed over the items to the firm's representative in Rohtak and was assured that they would be delivered within 10-15 days. He paid Rs 18,400 for a shipment weighing 21 kg through UPI.
However, the complainant said the items were not delivered within the promised period. He claimed that the clothes were meant for the winter season and would become useless after the season ended. 
The edible and perishable items also became stale or unusable because of the delay. He valued the items at Rs 50,000.
The complainant said he contacted the firm several times but did not receive a satisfactory response. He also sent a legal notice on February 27, 2025, but received no relief.
He approached the commission seeking Rs 3 lakh for non-delivery within the promised period, Rs 50,000 as compensation for harassment and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.
Brand House did not appear before the commission despite receiving notice. It was proceeded against ex parte through an order dated May 22, 2025, and did not file its defence.
Why commission held courier firm liable
The bench comprising president 
Nagender Singh Kadian and members 
Dr Tripti Pannu and 
Dr Vijender Singh noted that the complainant had submitted payment details, shipment documents, delivery receipt and WhatsApp conversations with the firm.
The commission observed that the WhatsApp chats showed that the firm had assured delivery of the perishable items within 10-12 days. However, the delivery receipt showed that the shipment was delivered only on February 28, 2025, after 28 days.
It said the delay could have made the perishable items stale, inedible or unusable. The clothes, too, could not serve their intended purpose because they were not delivered during the relevant season.
The bench also noted that the firm had failed to appear despite service of notice, leaving the complainant's evidence unrebutted.
“Perusal of the documents reveals that the items were delivered on 28.02.2025, i.e. after 28 days, as against the assured delivery period of 10-12 days. Due to such delay, the perishable items might have become stale, inedible or otherwise unusable. Further, the clothes, having not been delivered within the stipulated time, could not serve the intended purpose of the consignee at the relevant time,” the commission said.
The commission further recorded that the complainant had submitted during arguments that the shipment included 10 kg of desi ghee laddus, valued at around Rs 30,000, considering the cost of desi ghee and dry fruits. He had also paid Rs 18,400 as courier charges.
Considering the delay and the resulting loss, the bench said it would be just and proper to award Rs 30,000 towards the value of the edible items and Rs 18,400 towards courier charges.
Final order
The commission allowed the complaint and directed Brand House to:
- Pay Rs 48,400 towards the value of the edible items and courier charges, along with 9 percent annual interest from March 27, 2025, until realisation.
- Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment.
- Pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.
- The firm has been directed to comply with the order within 30 days of receiving a copy of it.

People walk past damaged homes near the shore at Uppada, in Kakinada, India, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026 after Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast.

stories.headline: Bengaluru man pays Rs 90,000 for Country Vacations holiday membership, seeks cancellation within six weeks without using any benefits; NCDRC calls company's reliance on 'no-refund' clause 'patently unfair and unjust' and orders full refund with 6% interest
stories.deck: A Bengaluru man paid Rs 90,000 for a holiday membership but sought cancellation within six weeks. Despite not using any benefits, the company refused to refund his payment due to a no-refund clause. The Karnataka State Consumer Commission ordered the refund with interest after ruling in his favor. Country Vacations and Country Club appealed to the NCDRC, which upheld the consumer commission's…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI/BENGALURU: A Bengaluru man who paid Rs 90,000 for a long-term holiday membership but sought to cancel it within six weeks without using any of its benefits is entitled to a refund, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has ruled. The commission held that refusing to cancel the membership by citing a contractual 'no-refund' clause, despite the consumer having availed no facilities, amounted to unfair and unjust conduct.
Dismissing a revision petition filed by Country Vacations and Country Club (India) Ltd, the NCDRC upheld an order of the Karnataka State Consumer Commission directing the companies to refund the membership fee with 6% annual interest and pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.
The complaint was filed by Sangeeth Bhadran, who received a promotional call from Country Vacations on December 2, 2013, offering holiday and vacation facilities and inviting him to visit its office. Five days later, Bhadran visited the company's Bengaluru office and signed a membership purchase agreement after being offered holiday benefits, accommodation facilities and discounts. He paid Rs 90,000 for the membership.
However, he later found that the benefits described during the promotional interaction did not match the actual terms and conditions of the agreement. He also alleged that he had been assured that maintenance charges would not apply to facilities he did not use. After examining the agreement, Bhadran sought cancellation and a refund of his money. Despite repeated emails, telephone calls and personal visits, the companies allegedly refused to cancel the membership or return the amount.
He subsequently approached the III Additional Bangalore Urban District Consumer Forum, which dismissed his complaint, finding no deficiency in service or unfair trade practice. Bhadran challenged the decision before the Karnataka State Consumer Commission, which ruled in his favour and directed the companies to refund Rs 90,000 with 6% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint until payment. It also awarded him Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.
Country Vacations and Country Club then approached the NCDRC, arguing that Bhadran had voluntarily entered into the agreement after understanding its terms, including the non-refundable nature of the membership fee. The companies said membership cards and gift vouchers had been issued to him, but he had neither attempted to use the holiday facilities nor paid the mandatory annual maintenance charges. They denied any misrepresentation or deficiency in service and argued that he had failed to produce evidence to support his allegations.
The NCDRC, however, observed that Bhadran's failure to use the membership facilities could not, by itself, absolve the companies of unfair conduct or validate one-sided contractual terms. It noted that he had been invited to the office, where the membership benefits were presented and the agreement signed on the same day. Within approximately one-and-a-half months, without availing any benefits, he sought to withdraw from the long-term arrangement.
 The commission held that refusing a refund by relying on the 'no-refund' clause, while continuing to impose an annual maintenance liability under the agreement was 'patently unfair and unjust'.
It observed that the companies could perhaps have deducted a proportionate amount for the one-and-a-half-month period, along with reasonable administrative charges or an earnest amount, before returning the balance. The commission said retaining the entire membership fee despite the consumer having availed no benefits would result in unjust and disproportionate enrichment of the companies.Finding no jurisdictional or other error in the Karnataka State Consumer Commission's order, the NCDRC dismissed the revision petition. The companies must now refund Bhadran's Rs 90,000 with 6% annual interest from the date of filing of the complaint until payment, besides paying Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.

stories.headline: Rs 8 vs Rs 24 per km: Why Bengaluru taxi drivers are protesting Green SM's entry
stories.deck: Taxi driver associations in Bengaluru are opposing Green SM's entry which could disrupt local livelihoods. The company reportedly plans to charge significantly lower fares than approved by the state government. Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh has halted further registrations of Green SM vehicles pending discussions. Many commuters support the new entrant, hoping for improved cab availability…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Taxi drivers' associations in Bengaluru have opposed the proposed entry of Vietnam-based electric mobility company Green SM into the city, claiming that its low fares could trigger a price war and threaten the livelihoods of thousands of local cab and autorickshaw operators.
The controversy centres on Green SM's reported plan to offer electric cab rides at around Rs 8 per kilometre, significantly lower than the Karnataka government's notified fare of Rs 24 per km for smaller taxis.
Drivers argue that independent operators, who have purchased vehicles through bank loans and bear the cost of EMIs, insurance, permits and maintenance, will struggle to compete with a company-backed fleet offering substantially lower fares.
Taxi drivers' associations in Bengaluru have opposed the proposed entry of Vietnam-based electric mobility company Green SM into the city
At least four taxi and transport associations have approached Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, seeking intervention over the company's proposed entry. In a representation, they urged the government to disclose details of the permissions and licences granted to Green SM and conduct an independent assessment of the potential economic impact on existing taxi and autorickshaw operators.
"We welcome the transition towards environmentally sustainable transportation. 
However, such a transition must be implemented in a fair, transparent and inclusive manner, without discriminating against local operators," the associations said.
Nataraj Sharma, president of the Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations, said the existing operators would find it difficult to match the proposed fares.
"Currently, there are no regulations from the state government on e-taxi fares. I think they can operate for less than Rs 8 per km. In Bengaluru, most taxis are running under petrol, diesel or CNG and autorickshaws use LPG as well. We will not be able to offer prices as low as them," he said.
The federation has argued that Green SM could have a competitive advantage because of its access to corporate capital, bulk vehicle purchases, its own app and fleet-management systems. It fears that independent drivers may be forced to reduce fares, struggle with loan repayments or eventually leave the business.
Taxi and autorickshaw associations have claimed that nearly eight lakh families in Bengaluru depend on the passenger transport sector for their livelihood. They have sought a cap on the company's fleet, an audit of its licence compliance and scrutiny of its fare structure.
The company, however, has denied reports that it charges Rs 8 per km, describing them as "inaccurate and unfounded". It said fare details are available through its official website and communication channels, while the app displays the fare before customers confirm a booking.
Government puts brakes on further registrations
Amid the opposition, Karnataka Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said the company had already secured registration for 100 taxis in the state capital. However, the Transport Department has directed regional transport officials not to register any additional Green SM vehicles until further orders.
The minister said the government had received information that the company was planning to register 10,000 electric taxis and charge between Rs 8 and Rs 10 per kilometre, which could affect the livelihoods of existing drivers.
"We have received information that they are planning to register 10,000 electric taxis and charge Rs 8 to Rs 10 per km. This will affect the livelihoods of people. I will discuss the issue with the chief minister. Representatives of the company had met me seeking permission. I have said no to them," Suresh said.
He added that a decision on allowing further registrations would be taken after discussions with Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, keeping the interests of local drivers in mind.
Green SM, meanwhile, has announced plans to expand its electric cab operations to Bengaluru and Chennai as part of a wider expansion across six Indian states and territories. The company is already operational in Delhi-NCR and Hyderabad.
Government-notified taxi fares
The dispute has also brought the state's existing taxi fare structure into focus. Under the Karnataka government's February 2024 notification, fares are determined by the cost of the vehicle.
- Cars costing up to Rs 10 lakh: Minimum fare of Rs 100 for the first 4km, followed by Rs 24 per km.
- Cars costing between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 15 lakh: Minimum fare of Rs 115 for the first 4km, followed by Rs 28 per km.
- Cars costing above Rs 15 lakh: Minimum fare of Rs 130 for the first 4km, followed by Rs 32 per km.
The notification also provides for a waiting charge of Re 1 per minute and an additional 10% charge for journeys booked between midnight and 6am.
Commuters divided over Green SM entry
While transport associations have raised concerns over the impact on local livelihoods, the proposed entry has also found support among some commuters, who believe increased competition could improve cab availability and bring down fares.
Several social media users have argued that passengers could benefit from having another operator in the city, particularly amid complaints about autorickshaw drivers refusing rides or not operating meters.
One user said more cab operators would give commuters greater choice, while another argued that the opposition was driven by commercial interests of existing players.

stories.headline: Karnataka embarks on aggressive AI skilling drive; to train 63,200 students, engineers
stories.bodyText:
To achieve this target, it exchanged Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) during the inaugural session of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) with five major technology firms: Google, Salesforce, Pega Systems, Sarvam AI, and Gnani.ai
The State government on Tuesday (November 17) announced an ambitious initiative to train 63,200 engineering students, diploma holders, and professionals in emerging Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies.
To achieve this target, it exchanged Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) during the inaugural session of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) with five major technology firms: Google, Salesforce, Pega Systems, Sarvam AI, and Gnani.ai.
These specialised skilling programmes will combine global expertise with homegrown AI capabilities, focusing on practical learning in Generative AI, Agentic AI, Voice AI, cloud computing, and Responsible AI, according to Karnataka’s IT & BT and Home Minister Priyank Kharge.
Highlighting the State’s vision, Mr. Kharge said, “Artificial Intelligence is reshaping industries, redefining jobs and creating new economic opportunities. Karnataka’s ambition is not just to participate in this transformation, but to help shape it.”
Explaining the scale of the State’s educational efforts, Kharge added, “Through initiatives such as Nipuna Karnataka and these industry partnerships, we are taking AI skilling to scale, with a proposed target of training over 63,000 students and engineers across the State.”
“Our focus is on ensuring that young people are equipped not merely to use AI tools, but to understand, develop and apply these technologies to solve real-world challenges,” he further said, adding, “By bringing together global technology leaders and homegrown AI innovators, we are building a talent ecosystem that is future-ready, industry-relevant and inclusive, while strengthening Karnataka’s position as a leading hub for AI innovation.”
The inaugural day concluded with a high-level panel discussion titled ‘AI & Beyond: The Emerging India’, moderated by Lingaraju Sawkar, president, Kyndryl India. During the session, Mr. Kharge detailed how Karnataka is deploying AI across governance, including chatbots for rural grievances, water quality monitoring, cybersecurity, and narcotics detection across roughly 5,000 police stations. He also spotlighted this government’s maiden initiative, which makes State departments — starting with the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board and the Home Department — the first customers for start-ups solving governance challenges.
Joining the panel, industry leaders weighed in on AI’s broader economic impact. Biocon Founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw highlighted AI’s transformative potential in biotechnology and healthcare, noting that it can connect complex biological data to accelerate drug discovery, diagnostics, and biomarker development, significantly reducing the time needed to bring a drug molecule from the laboratory to patients for personalised medicine.
Kris Gopalakrishnan, co-founder of Infosys and Chairman of Axilor Ventures, observed that while traditional IT services will remain relevant, AI allows firms to reimagine applications and build new products, driving demand for hardware and data centres. Addressing software jobs, he noted that because coding is heavily impacted by AI, professionals must increasingly focus on reviewing, validating, and certifying AI-generated code.
Meanwhile, Prashanth Prakash stressed moving beyond incremental changes toward outcome-driven innovation. He noted that AI enables businesses to deliver better services at lower costs, underscoring that data is a critical resource governments must leverage alongside computing capabilities to deliver solutions at scale in sectors like manufacturing and agriculture.

stories.headline: Karnataka: Farmers may have to wait a year or more to grow new crop varieties of ragi, maize and amaranth
stories.deck: These new varieties include Ragi GPU 101 which is an improved variety of MR-322, Maize MAH-20-45, an improved variety of MAH-14-5, and Grain Amaranth KBGA-18, an improved variety of KBGA-15.
stories.bodyText:
In light of the drought issue across Karnataka, three new crop varieties of ragi, maize and grain amaranth developed at the University of Agriculture Sciences-Bengaluru (UAS-B) were launched at the ongoing Krishi Mela. However, scientists who were involved in developing these varieties, as well as experts from other institutions, stated that it would take a year or two for these varieties to be available in the market for farmers to purchase.
These new varieties include Ragi GPU 101 which is an improved variety of MR-322, Maize MAH-20-45, an improved variety of MAH-14-5, and Grain Amaranth KBGA-18, an improved variety of KBGA-15. Scientists said that even before these varieties reach the market, it would take time to multiply seeds in large numbers, test them in various locations and weather conditions, get the varieties notified and approved by the respective organisations at the national and State levels.
Mudalagiriyappa D.R., Director of Research at UAS-B, said, “Though the new varieties have been launched, they are not available for farmers to purchase from the open market and cultivate. It will take a year or more for these crop varieties to be made fully available to the farmers in large numbers. A national indent has to be placed by the Ministry of Agriculture so that seeds of these crop varieties can be multiplied and made available to farmers across the country.”
Meanwhile, Sujata Bhat, Senior Technical Assistant, UAS-B, also stated that it took nearly 13 years for the university to develop Ragi GPU-101. Pointing towards the fresh yield of GPU-101 exhibited at Krishi Mela, she said, “The yield is 27% more when compared to the yield in the existing variety MR-322. But it has to be tested successfully for private companies to come forward and multiply seeds in large numbers.”
Uday Kumar, technical manager at the Institute of Agricultural Technologists, said, “The National Seed Corporation (NSC) under the government of India will take up large-scale multiplication of improved and notified crop varieties. Anything that the Ministry of Agriculture notifies, those varieties will be multiplied by NSC and sold to the farmers. Agriculture universities
He also noted that the university and the State Agriculture Department must work in coordination to forecast drought conditions, El Nino impact and crops that farmers are supposed to cultivate during such conditions. “If the forecasting is perfect then such crop varieties can be tested and released in large quantities,” he added.

briefs.headline: 40-year-old Bengaluru man slapped in road-rage spat, dies
briefs.deck: A call centre employee tragically died following a road-rage incident in Bengaluru due to a toddler running onto the road. William was returning home after attending a wedding when the confrontation occurred at night. An argument broke out between William and the suspected father after he avoided hitting the child. After being slapped, William collapsed and was later declared dead at the hospital.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A 40-year-old call centre staffer died after he was slapped by a man in a road-rage incident triggered by a toddler running onto the road in Hennur, east Bengaluru, last week.
William, from KSFC Layout in Lingarajapuram, was returning home after attending a wedding along with his friend and brother-in-law when a toddler dangerously sprinted on to the road around 11.45pm on Nov 13.
According to police, Dinesh, a resident of Horamavu, was travelling on a motorcycle along with Pradeep, who was in the middle, and William riding pillion. The incident took place near a fuel station on Hennur Main Road.
To avoid hitting the toddler, Dinesh applied the brakes. A man, suspected to be the child's father, rushed towards them, picked up the child and got into an argument with Dinesh, a police officer said.
With both sides allegedly hurling abuses, William got down from the motorcycle and confronted the man before slapping him in a fit of rage. This triggered a heated confrontation, with the man's family members joining in the fight and shouting at William.
In retaliation, the man allegedly slapped William, following which the latter collapsed and lost consciousness, Dinesh stated in his complaint. Dinesh and Pradeep rushed William to hospital where he was declared brought dead.
He worked with a private bank in Bannerghatta and is survived by his wife and two children.
CCTV from fuel station unclear: Police
Based on Dinesh's complaint, police registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Police said CCTV footage from the fuel station was unclear and the body has been sent for postmortem.
Police said they had identified the alleged assailant and warned him against leaving the city without informing the investigating officer.

briefs.headline: How Bengaluru man's meeting with pal turned fatal; gunned down in car
briefs.deck: In a chilling incident, Imraz Pasha, a Bengaluru scrap dealer, was found shot dead in his car early Tuesday. Last seen with a friend shortly before his death, a heated argument reportedly took place between them. As his family grew concerned after he failed to return home, police now suspect the friend may play a crucial role in this murder investigation.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A 45-year-old scrap dealer who was meeting a business associate on Monday afternoon was found shot dead in his hatchback car in east Bengaluru on Tuesday morning, with multiple bullet injuries to his head.
Police identified the deceased as Imraz Pasha, a resident of Bannerghatta Road. He was found dead in the front seat of the car in Papanna Layout, Manchappanahalli village.
Preliminary investigations said a passerby noticed the parked car with a dead man inside. He alerted police around 9.30am.
Joint commissioner of police (east) Ramesh Banoth said the deceased appeared to have sustained a gunshot wound to the right side of his head. Three bullets were fired at him, with two exit wounds found. A spent bullet cartridge was next to the car.
According to Pasha’s son, he and his father had taken up welding work near Bagaluru. While they were at work, one of Pasha’s friends from KP Agrahara asked him to meet.
Licensed pistol used in killing?
Pasha left around 2.30pm. An hour later, he called his son and said his friend was ‘talking nonsense’ and was getting into a verbal altercation with him.
After 5pm, Pasha’s son tried calling him, but there was no response. He later contacted his father’s friend, who reportedly told him that he had already left the place while Pasha had stayed back to meet someone else.
Pasha did not return home that night. His family members tried in vain to trace him. On Tuesday morning, when the son called the friend in the morning, he had blocked his number. Before the family could approach the police, Bagaluru police contacted them and informed them about his death.
Police suspect a friend who had called him for a meeting was behind the murder and are making efforts to arrest him.
Licensed pistol used in killing?
Police said the prime suspect possessed a licensed pistol and the same weapon had been used in shooting down Pasha around 4.30pm Monday.
Scene-of-crime officers and fingerprint collected evidence. Investigators are questioning family members to ascertain whether Pasha had any financial disputes or monetary dealings with the suspect or anyone else that could have led to the crime.
Pasha is survived by his parents, wife and children. Police are verifying the documents of the Belagavi-registered car.

briefs.headline: Work pressure, lack of sleep & proper food taking toll on crew of Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation bus: Study
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Braving overcrowded buses, jostling through passengers, managing the daily rush and remaining on their feet for hours, women conductors of the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) shoulder a demanding job that leaves little room for respite. A study by the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bengaluru, has found that women conductors have a higher average body mass index (BMI), waist circumference and body fat percentage.
The study, titled Assessment of Body Composition of Bengaluru Bus Conductors, was displayed at the ongoing Krishi Mela 2026. Conducted by the department of food science and nutrition at the Gandhi Krishi Vignana Kendra (GKVK), it examined 100 conductors — 50 men and 50 women — from BMTC depots 11 and 29 in Yelahanka during the first half of 2025. The study by Vedashri KN, an MSc graduate, under the guidance of department head Prof Usha Ravindra and Prof Chandrakala, found female conductors recorded an average BMI of 27, while men recorded 25.
More strikingly, their average body fat percentage stood at 36%, against 23% among male conductors. While male conductors recorded an average weight of 73kg and height of 168cm, their female counterparts weighed 66kg and measured 156cm on average. 
The study also highlighted concerns over inadequate sleep and bone density problems among several crew members.
Prof Usha Ravindra said many women conductors reported malnourishment, digestive problems and frequent urinary tract infections. “Due to work pressure, erratic shifts and prolonged working hours, they often fail to eat on time. Even when they manage to find time, they tend to grab whatever is available, which is often neither nutritious nor of good quality. These irregular eating habits have contributed to an increase in adipose tissue mass. Since it is difficult to find washrooms during their trips, many women also deliberately avoid drinking water throughout their shifts,” she said.
Pointing to the additional burden women shoulder beyond their workplace responsibilities, Prof Usha said they often had to manage both professional and domestic duties, leaving them with little time to look after their health.
Highlights of Krishi MelaJaffarabadi giant, the show stopper
Jaffarabadi breed buffalo, weighing 1250kg, on display at the Krishi mela at GKVK in Bengaluru
A massive Jaffarabadi breed buffalo (also known as Bhavnagri or Gir) weighing a staggering 1,250kg has emerged as the star attraction at the annual Krishi Mela. Originating from the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, the breed is among India’s heaviest buffalo varieties. Valued at over Rs 6 lakh, Jaffarabadi buffaloes are prized for their rich milk, which contains 8% to 12% fat.
Honey on a spoon!
Students from Chintamani College of Agriculture have come up with an innovative concept of selling pre-packed honey in spoons under the brand name ‘Honey Nova’. The 10 ml single-use packs are priced between Rs 10 and Rs 20. Each spoon is filled with honey and sealed with silver foil, which can simply be peeled off before consumption. The ready-to-use format eliminates the hassle of handling sticky bottles, repeated opening and closing, and concerns over hygiene, according to Srushti SN and Harshitha CG, students who developed the product.
Ornamental Sunflower
Visitors walk past flower beds, vegetable plots, and insect displays during the annual four-day Krishi Mela 2026, organised by the University of Agricultural Sciences
With Bengaluru witnessing a growing demand for sunflowers in interior floral decorations, bouquets and ceremonial arrangements, an ornamental sunflower variety developed by UAS is attracting considerable attention from farmers at the agricultural fair. Agricultural scientists said the ornamental variety could fetch farmers up to 10 times the income generated by conventional sunflower varieties.
White Marigold
A white marigold variety named ‘Vanilla’, developed by the department of horticulture at the UAS, is yet another major attraction. It offers a yield of 15 to 20 tonnes per hectare, while the harvested flowers can be stored for up to two weeks.

briefs.headline: Dodged CCTV at stations, rode 2,000 km across 4 states on bike: How Bengaluru murder accused was nabbed in Bihar
briefs.deck: Amit Kumar Dubey became a prime suspect in the murder of advocate Manjunath in Whitefield. He traveled over 2,000 kilometers on a motorcycle to avoid being detected by authorities and surveillance cameras. His journey included stops in Hyderabad, Nagpur, Varanasi, and finally Bihar, where he blended into rural life. Police investigated his movements and analyzed call records to identify his…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Desperate to evade the dragnet of highway and transit surveillance, a suspect in last month’s sensational murder of a Whitefield advocate travelled at least 2,000 km across four states on a commuter motorcycle, only to be tracked down working as a daily-wage farmhand in a remote Bihar village.
Amit Kumar Dubey, one of the two prime suspects accused of gunning down advocate 
Manjunath
 in Whitefield last month, was arrested last Friday by a police team in Nanauri village, located in the Dhanarua block of Patna district.
When investigators finally caught up with him and asked why he had opted for an exhausting five-to-six-day road journey on a Hero Honda Splendor instead of taking public transport, Dubey reportedly gave a straightforward answer: “I was aware that there are CCTV cameras at bus stands and railway stations, and police would easily catch me.”
The cross-country escape
Probe revealed that immediately after the crime, Dubey packed a single backpack with clothes, a charger, and electronic gadgets. Wearing a jacket and a full-face helmet to conceal his identity, he set off northwards, riding from daybreak until nightfall and surviving on meals at roadside eateries.
His escape route spanned roughly five to six days
- Hyderabad (around 575 km from Bengaluru): Dubey’s first major halt, where he sold one of his mobile handsets at a throwaway price to raise cash and spent the night sleeping at a railway station.
- Nagpur (around 500 km from Hyderabad): After riding north from Telangana into Maharashtra, he rested overnight at a local bus stand.
- Nagpur to Varanasi –Around 730 km.
- Varanasi to Bihar (around 230 km): Crossing into Uttar Pradesh and eventually Bihar, he avoided hotels, opting instead to pay Rs 200–300 a night for a rope cot (charpai) at roadside dhabas.
- Upon reaching Patna district, Dubey sought shelter with a distant maternal relative in Nanauri. Keeping a low profile, he blended into rural life by taking up work as an agricultural labourer on his relative’s farm for Rs 400 a day.
Despite his attempts to evade surveillance, Dubey’s solo journey was captured by several highway CCTV cameras along the Bengaluru–Hyderabad–Nagpur corridor. 
The trail briefly went cold beyond Nagpur, where surveillance infrastructure along the highway was sparse. However, investigators secured a crucial breakthrough when footage from a fuel station on the outskirts of Varanasi confirmed that he was heading towards Bihar.
Meanwhile, an analysis of Dubey’s past call detail records (CDRs) revealed that he was in frequent contact with his grandmother, who lives in Nanauri. Suspecting that he might eventually return to his native village, police had raided the area shortly after the murder but returned empty-handed.
Keeping the village under discreet surveillance, a team of officers in plain clothes finally moved in last Friday. They tracked Dubey to the agricultural fields where he was working and apprehended him before he could flee.
Police are still searching for the prime suspect, 
Pavan
, who allegedly shot the advocate dead.

briefs.headline: Salon employee molests Bengaluru woman during hair spa, arrested
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A routine visit to a salon for a hair spa turned into a distressing ordeal for a 31-year-old woman after an employee allegedly touched her inappropriately during the session on Nov 12.
The complainant, 
Sarita
 (name changed) from Rajajinagar, an employee of a private firm, approached Basaveshwaranagar police Nov 13, a day after the incident.
Sarita had visited Aativa Salon near Rajajinagar Industrial Township, reportedly owned by an actress-cum-reality show participant, for a hair spa. Between 6.40pm and 7.10pm, an employee identified as Arsalangazhi allegedly misbehaved with her while giving her a massage.
She alleged that he deliberately slipped his hands inside her T-shirt and touched her inappropriately. Sarita asked him twice to stop and explicitly instructed him to limit the service to washing her hair. However, Arsalangazhi allegedly asked whether he could massage her hands and later her back, both of which she declined. Only after she reiterated her instructions two to three times did the employee finally proceed to wash and dry her hair.
 Sarita then paid the bill and left the salon.
A police officer said a case had been registered under Section 75 (sexual harassment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at Basaveshwaranagar police station.
Arsalangazhi, 24, has been arrested and subsequently released on station bail. He claimed that he had massaged only the woman’s shoulders and denied other allegations.
When TOI contacted the salon, a staff member declined to comment, saying police were handling the matter.

briefs.headline: What a Guns N’ Roses concert feels like in 2026
briefs.deck: As Guns N’ Roses performed in Bengaluru after 14 years, fans revelled in a wave of nostalgia and the chance to catch their rock legends up close
briefs.bodyText:
Telling people you’re attending a Guns N’ Roses in concert in 2026 is likely to evoke two kinds of responses — an enthusiastic ‘Wow!’ about catching one of the greatest rock bands of yore or a dismissive ‘Nah’ for aged icons soldiering on despite shortcomings such as Axl Rose’s vocal performances in recent years.
Playing in the city after 14 years, what made it count was it was the first time with original members (and stars in their own right), Slash and Duff McKagan joining Axl, longtime pianist and keyboardist Dizzy Reed, guitarist Richard Fortus and newly inducted drummer Isaac Carpenter.
They performed in Mumbai last year and similarly, some chose not to attend out of wanting to keep their memories of the band’s heyday intact. Others just wanted to have a good time and perhaps tick off their bands-to-watch bucketlist.
I walked into NICE Grounds after taking a Metro train that was heavily populated with concert-goers in black T-shirts. With just a QR code entry at the turnstile, there were no wristbands at this show. It meant that was one less keepsake memory from the show, although I’ll always have the videos and photos from the concert.
As Girish And The Chronicles (GATC) kicked off the concert with tracks from their new album Disintegrate, frontman Girish Pradhan also obliged the crowd clamouring for one of his signature vocal exercises during soundcheck. Considering they’ve been supporting Guns N’ Roses in India and even Abu Dhabi, over the last few years, GATC dialled things up with powerful, fist-pumping rock.
It took over an hour and a half before Guns N’ Roses (GnR) took the stage. With over 15,000 in attendance, there was so much to observe — there were people donning a top hat a la Slash, others had tied red bandanas around their heads — pointing to the pop culture impact GnR has had for decades now.
It was heartening to see people aged from 10 to 70 in the audience, all having different memories of the band — some through cassettes and CDs, others through music videos and family playlists on streaming platforms.
Kshama Ravikumar was attending with her husband Ashwin Sameeran and 10-year-old son Agni. She says, “My introduction to Guns N’ Roses was watching ‘November Rain’ on MTV.” Asked if her son has seen the video, she laughs and says, “He’s a bit shy about kissing scenes, so he hasn’t watched the video but he listens to quite a bit of rock.”
While Agni can’t wait for ‘Welcome To The Jungle’ (he’s dressed in a white T-shirt picturising the song), Kshama is excited about the other classics, “I want to listen to ‘Sweet Child o’ Mine’ and ‘November Rain’, that is one of the best love songs ever.” Ashwin says they missed seeing the band in Mumbai last year, and wanted to seize this opportunity. “Who knows if they’ll come back again? After this, we don’t know,” he says.
Kshama, like a few fans I spoke to, is forgiving of the fact that Axl Rose doesn’t sound like the most versatile vocalist in rock music, which he used to be. She counters with a laugh. “Well, we’ve grown older, so they’ve grown older, so we’re very forgiving. But, you know, they are icons, they are legends. We are just happy to be part of that.”
Elsewhere, another man spots my T-shirt (of the nu-metal band Korn) and gets talking about why he’s here. His children are here for an initiation of sorts because they also play music. On my ride back on the Metro, I hear another parent explaining why they brought their child along. “My son, who is a teenager, is playing the guitar and I wanted him to see GnR so that he would be inspired.”
On that front, there was not much lacking at all, courtesy of Slash and Richard Fortus. Shredding all over, beads of sweat just made Slash look every bit a gladiator, as he dug into legendary songs such as ‘Welcome To The Jungle’, their incendiary rendition of ‘Live and Let Die’ and ‘Civil War’. Slash even got his own guitar solo section, occasionally dipping into blues with a bit of ‘Voodoo Chile’ by Jimi Hendrix.
The solo everyone was waiting for, of course, was part of ‘November Rain’. A grand piano was wheeled on stage and Axl Rose sat down and began the legendary rock ballad, and everyone in the audience turned singer.
Riju Dasgupta, a Mumbai-based musician who performs under the moniker Dr Hex, was catching GnR for the third time and ‘November Rain’ was a standout. “I remember the exact moment when I saw Slash walk out of the church and play that solo in the music video, and this time they had a different backdrop with water falling and everything. I found that incredibly moving,” he recalls after the Bengaluru concert.
Discovering GnR around 2000 after seeing the music video for ‘Estranged’ on MTV, Riju had found a new favourite band right then. Like anyone else in India who has a bucketlist of bands, he never thought he’d see GnR. Compared to last year’s performance in Mumbai, he feels Axl Rose and the band have worked on their craft a bit more and “are more disciplined and in better spirits”.
By comparison, Samantak Bhadra, a regular concert-goer, was seeing them for the first time after having heard them from his school days. He says he attended without having too many expectations, but walked away in awe. “Once a hero, always a hero. GnR was instrumental in shaping my love and passion for rock music. Nostalgia is a big part of why I went. But more than that, I went there as a 16-year-old, wide-eyed kid unable to believe the fairytale he was living in,” Bhadra says.
Axl moved like a man possessed when ‘Welcome To The Jungle’ kicked off their set, another fast paced classic ‘Bad Obsession’ followed and he acknowledged (with a bit of expletive language) how good it felt to be back on stage in Bengaluru. Heavy metal havoc followed with ‘It’s So Easy’ and there was the galloping hair metal of ‘Mr. Brownstone’.
A delightful surprise was the band launching into ‘Slither’ by Velvet Revolver, a supergroup that Slash and Duff McKagan were part of with late vocalist Scott Weiland. Few people recognised the song, but those who did chanted along.
Songs like ‘Chinese Democracy’ to ‘Yesterdays’ and ‘Estranged’, saw Axl Rose having the time of his life, twirling around on stage with his mic stand. It felt like being strapped into a hard rock rollercoaster that twisted and turned and looped into epic scale composing. They slowed things down with their rendition of ‘Wichita Lineman’ and it gave Axl a chance to indulge in a bit of teasing. He said they would bring out a special guest and everyone’s anticipation levels were raised, but all he did was reintroduce Slash on the pedal steel guitar, and laughter filled the air.
Standing about 20 feet away from the stage, it was incredible to see these greats up close. Looking around me, I felt like I was the only one who thought that way, because many at my distance from the stage still preferred to crane upwards to the nearby LED where the camera was capturing closeups.
After a powerful, high octane guitar solo section that got all the phones out to record, without missing a beat, GnR introduced ‘Sweet Child o’ Mine’ with Slash playing the iconic riff. The audience didn’t miss a word, swaying along. It felt like being at a karaoke or Pecos on a weekend. All the band needed to do was play the song.
Upping the stakes for the final stretch, GnR ran through the nostalgia-drenched ‘November Rain’, with Slash up on an elevated section of the stage that had a railing and ‘Don’t Cry’, which admittedly wasn’t Rose’s best moment of the night, because a ballad needs to be carried off by the vocalist. A surprise cover of Aerosmith’s ‘Seasons of Wither’ indicated just how much GnR are about making these concerts fun for themselves, several decades on.
Switching up guitars at least half a dozen times, Slash slung a double neck guitar for ‘Knockin on Heaven’s Door’ and although it is also a Bob Dylan cover, GnR have made it their own. I look around and it is one of the most heartwarming sights of the night — people with their arms around friends, singing and swaying along.
The night ended with ‘Paradise City’, one of their more glamourous, aspirational songs and that is as good as it gets when you want to close on a high.
Published - November 17, 2026 07:17 pm IST

briefs.headline: Karnataka Lokayukta directs Bengaluru West City Corporation Commissioner to fix accountability for inaction on illegal construction
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner of the Bengaluru West City Corporation to identify officials responsible for failing to act against an unauthorised construction in Rajarajeshwari Nagar and initiate appropriate action against those found responsible.
The direction follows a complaint filed by K. Manjunath of Ramachandrapura, alleging that officials of the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), now part of the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s Bengaluru West City Corporation, failed to take action against illegal construction at Site No. 67 in Ward No. 160 of the Rajarajeshwarinagar Sub-Division.
According to the complaint, the property owner, N.S. Balachandra Dutta, had obtained building permission for a basement, ground floor and two upper floors. However, the owner allegedly proceeded to construct two additional floors in violation of the sanctioned plan and building bye-laws.
Despite the issuance of notices under Sections 248(1), 248(2) and 248(3) of the BBMP Act, 2020, followed by a confirmation order under Section 356(1) on September 3, 2024, the unauthorised construction was allegedly not removed.
The authority noted that no effective steps had been taken to execute the confirmation order. Despite repeated directions, reminders, and a show-cause notice, the Executive Engineer concerned also failed to submit an action-taken report.
Executive Engineer S.L. Papireddy, who appeared before the authority on Monday (November 16) in response to a summons, stated that the order issued under Section 356(1) had not been communicated to him.
Taking serious note of the continued inaction, the Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner to examine the matter, identify the officials responsible for the lapses, fix accountability and initiate appropriate action against the erring officials.
The Commissioner has been directed to appear in person before the authority on December 7 and submit a detailed report.

stories.headline: Rupee rises 24 paise to 93.27 against U.S. dollar in early trade
stories.deck: Forex traders said the appreciation in the rupee was primarily fuelled by a steep overnight drop in Brent crude oil prices, which eases India's import bill and inflation concerns
stories.bodyText:
The rupee appreciated 24 paise to 93.27 against the U.S. dollar in early trade on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), supported by declining crude prices and surging foreign portfolio inflows into Indian equities.
Forex traders said the appreciation in the rupee was primarily fuelled by a steep overnight drop in Brent crude oil prices, which eases India's import bill and inflation concerns.
Moreover, robust foreign institutional inflows — exceeding $8 billion into Indian equities so far this month — and a broad rally in domestic stock benchmarks enthused investors.
At the interbank forex market, the domestic unit opened at 93.47 against the greenback and gained ground to touch 93.27, registering a rise of 24 paise over its previous close.
On Tuesday, the rupee gained 43 paise to close at its seven-month high of 93.51 against the U.S. dollar.
"The rupee's gains have been mainly on account of falling oil and FPIs inflows which have taken share market also up and the gains may continue till 92.80 a strong support for the dollar," Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.60, higher by 0.12 per cent.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.46% lower at $92.71 per barrel in futures trade.
According to Anindya Banerjee, Head of Commodity and Currency Research, Kotak NEO, exceptional foreign inflows and lower crude are overwhelming the strength of the global dollar.
"Until the dollar trend changes, I would respect the prevailing direction across commodities rather than try to anticipate a bottom prematurely," he said.
On the domestic equity market front, Sensex declined 75.10 points to 82,482.30 in early trade; Nifty fell 26.95 points to 25,355.65.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹4,195.38 crore on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to exchange data.

stories.headline: DRI searches Cipla’s Mumbai office and Bhiwandi depot over imported drug classification
stories.deck: The pharmaceutical company said it cooperated with authorities and that the search would have no material impact on its financials or operations
stories.bodyText:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Mumbai zonal unit, has conducted searches at pharmaceutical company Cipla’s office in Vikhroli and its depot in Bhiwandi, Thane, over the classification or exemption of an imported finished pharmaceutical product. The searches were conducted on Monday under Section 105 of the Customs Act, 1962.
In a regulatory filing under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, Cipla said the proceedings were related to the classification or exemption of the imported pharmaceutical product. The company confirmed that it had extended full cooperation and assistance to the authorities during the searches.
Cipla said the proceedings would have no material impact on its financials, operations or other activities. The filing did not provide further details about the product or the specific classification issue under examination.
Cipla shares were trading at ₹1,390.70 on the BSE, down 0.24 per cent.
